notes.title: Quarterly planning offsite
notes.body:
Quarterly planning offsite — notes from the three days.

Day one was mostly alignment on priorities. We agreed to focus on reliability before new features, and to cut the number of active projects from nine to five. Marketing wants a clearer launch calendar, and engineering asked for two quiet weeks in every cycle to pay down technical debt. Nobody objected to either.

Hiring: we will open two senior backend roles and one designer role. Interviews run in the first half of the month so offers can land before the budget review. The recruiter will share a shortlist every Friday. We also discussed referral bonuses and decided to keep them as they are for now.

Logistics for the cabin stay: check-in is after 4pm, the host leaves firewood by the porch, and the wifi password for the cabin is lakehouse42 (network name is PineRidge). Quiet hours start at 10pm. Bring your own towels and a battery pack because the power can drop in the evening.

Day two covered the roadmap. The onboarding rewrite moves to next quarter, search quality work stays, and the billing cleanup is shared between two teams. We reviewed the incident log and agreed on a simple rule: every outage gets a written review within a week, no blame, with one concrete follow-up owner.

Closing remarks and action items: send the revised roadmap by Monday, book the venue for the next offsite, and collect feedback from everyone on how the three days went. Overall mood was positive and focused.
